correctness.rationale: For all odd integers \(n\ge3\), quotient graph neighborhoods have size \(n\) and distinct neighborhood intersections of size zero or two. Unique centers for faces of size at least three give an explicit acyclic toggle matching with no critical cells above dimension two. Matsushita Theorems 1.1/3.2 apply: the square-filled graph complex is the antipodal quotient of the simply connected cubical two-skeleton, with fundamental group \(\mathbb Z/2\) and an odd-length generator; its even subgroup, hence the neighborhood-complex fundamental group, is trivial. Face counts yield rank \(2^{n-3}(n^2-5n+8)-1\) for reduced degree-two integral homology and no other reduced homology. Invariant simplices under any nonzero translation are either absent or exactly \(2^{n-2}\) transposed edges, giving traces \(-1\) or \(2^{n-2}-1\); exact finite Fourier inversion gives every displayed multiplicity. Executed package scripts reproduce face vectors, chain ranks, fixed-simplex traces and every character for dimensions 3,5,7 and further symbolic multiplicity sums. All claims concern a stated infinite range proved by argument, not extrapolation from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The precise contribution is the full rational translation-character decomposition for all odd folded cubes, not the nonequivariant homology rank. Matsushita 2012/2017 supplies a fundamental-group theorem only; Csorba 2008 concerns simple equivariant equivalences of graph-complex constructions under a distinguished involution, not an explicit translation module in the accessible abstract. An existing nonequivariant folded-cube homotopy classification does not determine its automorphism action: many rational representations share the same dimension. Exact searches for translation modules, weight-two Fourier character formulas, aliases and broader graph-family results did not produce an implication proving the statement. One equivariant graph-complex paper was inspectable only through its abstract, and unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: The translation subgroup is intrinsic to the folded cubes and acts faithfully on their graph vertices; rational character multiplicities describe which symmetries preserve or reverse homology classes. These multiplicities differ sharply by weight (e.g., at dimension five: 6, 1 and 3), information unavailable from Betti numbers, Euler characteristic or nonequivariant sphere wedges. The theorem is a natural complete all-odd-dimensional family classification, derived from fixed-simplex geometry and the low-dimensional topology, not a parameter-shift computation.
